stories.headline: Cyclone Arnab: APEPDCL opens 41 control rooms, keeps 4,056 workers ready to restore power
stories.title: Cyclone Arnab: APEPDCL opens 41 control rooms, keeps 4,056 workers ready to restore power
stories.summary: People in Kakinada, East Godavari and Konaseema, the districts likely to bear the brunt, can report power problems on helpline 1912
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Andhra Pradesh Eastern Power Distribution Company Limited (APEPDCL) has stepped up its preparedness for Cyclone Arnab and is concentrating on Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema, Godavari and Kakinada districts, towards which the storm is expected to make landfall.

Following the India Meteorological Department (IMD)’s warning about Cyclone Arnab over the east-central and adjoining south-east Bay of Bengal, the utility has mobilised personnel, machinery and electrical materials to minimise disruptions and speed up power restoration in affected areas.
APEPDCL has opened 30 divisional control rooms, in addition to 11 circle-level control rooms, to monitor the situation and coordinate emergency response.
Kakinada and East Godavari have three divisional control rooms each, and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema has two.
A separate cell has been established at the corporate office to coordinate manpower deployment round the clock under the supervision of the Chief General Manager (Operations and Customer Service).
APEPDCL CMD I. Prudhvi Tej held a teleconference with senior engineering officials to review cyclone preparedness.
The utility has also sought 150 teams of 10 personnel each from the Southern Power Distribution Company of Andhra Pradesh Limited (APSPDCL) and requested additional materials from it.
The utility has arranged 394 contractor teams comprising 4,056 personnel for emergency response and restoration work.
The available resources include 211 diesel generator sets, 273 pole-drilling machines, 517 power saws and 318 earth movers and cranes.
A fleet of 366 departmental and private vehicles has been listed to transport personnel and materials to affected locations.
Another 100 mobile handsets have been arranged for communication during emergency operations.
APEPDCL said it had stocks of conductors, cables, distribution transformers and electric poles as of October 25.

stories.headline: Cyclone Arnab threatens Andhra’s municipal polls; SEC hopes to hold them on schedule
stories.title: Cyclone Arnab threatens Andhra’s municipal polls; SEC hopes to hold them on schedule
stories.summary: State Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha expects normalcy within two days of the storm crossing the coast
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: As Cyclone Arnab is closing in on the Andhra Pradesh coast and likely to affect the conduct of elections to urban local bodies (ULBs) on November 1, State Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha discussed it with State Disaster Management Authority Managing Director Prakhar Jain to gear up for any contingency.

Mr. Punetha told The Hindu that the cyclone appeared to be severe as per the information provided by Mr. Jain, and the Commission was monitoring the system brewing in the Bay of Bengal, which is predicted to make landfall on October 28.
He expressed confidence that the government would bring the situation to normalcy within two days after the cyclone crossed the coast, thereby facilitating the conduct of ULB polls on schedule.

But if the cyclone proves to be as devastating as it is expected to be, the Commission would then take a decision on conducting the elections, Mr. Punetha said, adding that he was keeping his fingers crossed for now.
Where the cyclone is now?
The deep depression in the Bay of Bengal strengthened into Cyclone Arnab (pronounced “Ornab”) early on Monday (October 26, 2026), the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said.
At 5.30 a.m. on Monday, it was about 650 km east-southeast of Visakhapatnam, 730 km from Kakinada, 830 km from Machilipatnam and 910 km from Bapatla, moving west at 15 kmph.
The IMD expects the storm to grow stronger by Monday midnight and stronger still on Tuesday.
It is likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam by the forenoon of Wednesday (October 28), with winds of 115 to 125 kmph gusting to 140 kmph.
The IMD has issued a red alert, its highest cyclone warning, for the Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha coasts.

stories.headline: Odisha bans fishing, tourist entry in 6 districts amid cyclone alert
stories.title: Odisha bans fishing, tourist entry in 6 districts amid cyclone alert
stories.summary: The government has mobilised its resources in Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Malkangiri, Koraput and Nabarangpur, the identified vulnerable districts of the southern region
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Odisha government has prohibited fishing activities in the sea and banned entry of tourists in the hills, waterfalls and dams in six districts as it has stepped up precautionary measures in view of a cyclonic storm that is likely to make landfall in neighbouring Andhra Pradesh within 48 hours, officials said on Monday (October 26, 2026).

The government has mobilised its resources in Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Malkangiri, Koraput and Nabarangpur, the identified vulnerable districts of the southern region, while Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi deputed eight ministers at separate places to monitor pre-cyclone activities, they said.

Rescue teams, comprising personnel of the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF), the Fire and Emergency Services, and the police, have been pre-positioned in vulnerable areas, the officials said.
The cyclonic storm, 'Arnab', is likely to make landfall along the neighbouring Andhra Pradesh coast on Wednesday (October 28, 2026), according to an IMD forecast.

The India Meteorological Department, in its bulletin on Monday (October 26, 2026) morning, said the deep depression over the Bay of Bengal moved nearly westwards with a speed of 15 kmph during the past six hours and intensified into a cyclonic storm.

“It is very likely to move west-northwestwards and intensify further into a severe cyclonic storm over west-central Bay of Bengal by midnight of October 26 and into a very severe cyclonic storm over the same region on October 27,” it said.

Odisha’s Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari said, "Although the system is expected to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast, the Odisha government would take no chances and remain fully prepared to deal with any eventuality."
After landfall, the weather system is projected to move to certain areas within Odisha's territory.
The State government is "fully prepared to tackle the situation", and therefore there is no reason to panic, the Minister said.

"Fishing activities in the sea have been completely prohibited, while tourist entry into hills, waterfalls, dams, and scenic destinations across the vulnerable six districts has also been banned," he said.
In view of inclement weather conditions, schools, colleges, and Anganwadi centres in these districts will remain closed on October 28 and 29.
The government has cancelled leave of its employees in the identified districts, and control rooms have been opened to coordinate relief and rescue operations, the Minister said.

stories.headline: Cyclone Arnab may take heavy rain regime away from South Peninsula
stories.title: Cyclone Arnab may take heavy rain regime away from South Peninsula
stories.summary: The building very severe cyclone is expected to track north-northeastwards, dragging a sprawling rain across large swathes eastern and central India, and away from most of the South Peninsula
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Sunday’s depression gathered steam at accelerated pace overnight on Monday and intensified twice over to become cycloneArnab, the first of this north-east monsoon, over the east-central and adjoining south-east Bay.
Moving at a brisk 15 km/hr early on Monday, the system is expected to intensify further into a very severe cyclone, putting the Andhra Pradesh coast squarely in the firing line.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) located the storm about 650 km east-south-east of Visakhapatnam; 730 km east-south-east of Kakinada; 830 km east of Machilipatnam; and 910 km east of Bapatla, all in Andhra Pradesh.
The cyclone is forecast to barrel west-north-west, strengthen into a severe cyclone over the west-central Bay by midnight and a very severe cyclonic storm over the same region on Tuesday.

It is then expected to swing north-westwards and cross the Andhra Pradesh-Yanam coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam by Wednesday morning, packing maximum sustained winds of 115-125 km/hr, gusting to 140 km/hr.
The cyclone’s landfall, however, will be far from the end of the story.
Although it will lose some punch after moving ashore, Arnab is expected to track north-north-eastwards, dragging a sprawling rain across large swathes of eastern and central India.

Extremely heavy to very heavy rainfall, with heavy spells in several areas, is forecast across Odisha, Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Bihar, West Bengal, Vidarbha, east Madhya Pradesh and east Uttar Pradesh over the three to four days beginning Wednesday.
The unfolding scenario could therefore shift the rain action away from much of the South Peninsula.

The heavy-rain regime that has held sway over large parts of Tamil Nadu and adjoining South Peninsula, barring southern Tamil Nadu and Kerala, may give way to Arnab and its northward march into the eastern farming heartland of the country and farther east, with its reach extending towards east Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal.
Chennai remained partly cloudy at 10 am, and may continue to remain same through the day today (Monday).
The sheer geographical spread of the rainfall threat reflects the system’s expected staying power.

stories.summary: Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge’s controversial remark about Prime Minister Narendra Modi has triggered a fresh political storm. Speaking at an event in Patna, Kharge reportedly said, “Modi ka baap bhi jayega,” after a man from the audience defended the Prime Minister. The man was allegedly beaten by Congress workers after the event, escalating the controversy. BJP leaders, including Union Home Minister Amit Shah and party chief Nitin Nabin, strongly condemned Kharge’s language, accusing him of crossing political decency. Congress leaders have defended their party chief. The incident has revived scrutiny of Kharge’s earlier controversial remarks about Modi, further intensifying the Congress-BJP war of words.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Criticises Tamil Nadu Govt For Dragging 1996 Riot Compensation Matter
stories.title: Supreme Court Criticises Tamil Nadu Govt For Dragging 1996 Riot Compensation Matter
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday pulled up the Tamil Nadu government for repeatedly seeking adjournments in a matter concerning compensation for property and business losses caused by communal riots of 1996 in Thoothukudi (Tuticorin), questioning its failure to ensure timely relief to the victims.

A bench comprising Justice SVN Bhatti and Justice NV Anjaria expressed displeasure over the State government's approach, observing that despite appointing commissions to address grievances following communal riots and arson, the authorities often fail to ensure that the promised relief reaches those affected.
"So tired of this matter, I think I will carry this through my demitting the office...
It is a simple matter; the State ought not to be dragging its feet," Justice Bhatti remarked after the bench was informed that a letter seeking an adjournment had been circulated last Saturday.
The matter dates back to 1996, when communal riots in Thoothukudi caused damage to businesses and properties.
Following the incident, the State government appointed a former District Judge as a one-man commission to assess the losses and recommend compensation to the affected persons.
The commission recommended compensation based on the actual losses suffered.
However, the State government subsequently issued Government Order G.O.Ms.No.1834, granting uniform compensation of Rs.
2 lakh to all affected persons.
The decision was challenged before the Madras High Court.
Both the Single Judge and the Division Bench favoured compensation in accordance with the recommendations of the one-man commission.
The State government subsequently challenged the High Court's decisions before the Supreme Court.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Refuses To Entertain Plea Seeking CBI Probe Against AIADMK MLAs Who Resigned To Join CM Vijay-Led TVK
stories.title: Supreme Court Refuses To Entertain Plea Seeking CBI Probe Against AIADMK MLAs Who Resigned To Join CM Vijay-Led TVK
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court today refused to entertain a writ petition against 5 MLAs of the All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK) who resigned and joined Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay-led Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) following the 2026 Tamil Nadu Assembly elections.
A bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana passed the order in a writ petition filed by one M Srinivasan.
Justice Bagchi orally observed that the issue of an MLA resigning to join another party was something political parties could look into and there is "nothing criminal" about it.
When the petitioner's counsel submitted that there's already an FIR registered, the judge replied, "then let the FIR be investigated.
Law will take its own course".

Briefly put, the petition sought directions to CBI to register an FIR against former AIADMK MLAs N Anand @ Bussy N Anand, K Maragatham Kumaravel, S Jayakumar, P Sathyabama and E Subaya alias Esakki Subaya for allegedly indulging in horse trading to prove majority in the TN Assembly.

stories.title: Maharashtra SIR: Supreme Court seeks ECI reply on voter deletions, denies claims deadline extension

article_sentences: The plea also challenges the use of Form 6 for voters already enrolled in previous elections.

New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Monday sought the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) response to a plea alleging large-scale deletion of voters from Maharashtra’s electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise, while declining to immediately extend the deadline for filing claims and objections.

A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana issued notice to the ECI on a petition filed by Arun Anandagiri, who alleged that 33% of voters had been deleted from the state’s electoral rolls during the SIR exercise.
The court, however, did not grant the petitioner’s request to extend the deadline on Monday.
The bench said it would consider extending the date if, after hearing the matter, it found that more time was required.
The case is scheduled to be heard next on November 5.
Senior Advocate Arvind Datar, appearing for Anandagiri, raised concerns over voters being left out of the rolls because of changes in their addresses and other details.
He told the court that around 3,500 redevelopment projects were underway in Mumbai and Pune, with old housing societies being demolished and thousands of residents being relocated.

According to the petitioner, such displacement could put voters at risk of losing their names from the electoral rolls if their current address or other details could not be matched during the revision process.
Datar also questioned the use of Form 6 for voters who were already enrolled in previous elections.
He argued that Form 6 is meant for registering new voters and that existing voters should not be required to use the same form to retain their names on the electoral rolls.
The petitioner sought a separate form or process for voters whose names had already appeared on earlier electoral rolls.

The Court however declined to pass ex parte orders to extend the date for claims and objections or to restrain the ECI from publishing the final voters' list.

Datar said that these deleted voters are asked by the ECI to file Form 6 to register as fresh voters.
He said that Form 6 is meant for first-time voters, and persons who have voted previously cannot be asked to fill Form 6.
He requested that the ECI be asked to not finalise the list(which is due on November 6), as Maharashtra does not have any immediate election.
He urged that it will take some time to bring back the 3 crore deleted voters.
"In Pune and Bombay, 40% voters are not there," Datar submitted.
He submitted that in these cities, many voters were relocated after redevelopment projects; however, the many of them were deleted on the ground "person not found."
He requested extending the date for final list publication, underscoring that it was a peculiar problem in Maharashtra.

stories.title: Supreme Court Permits Ashish Mishra To Visit Lakhimpur Kheri For Diwali
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday heard the bail-related proceedings of Ashish Mishra, son of former Union Minister Ajay Mishra Teni, in the Lakhimpur Kheri violence case and allowed him permission to visit his hometown to celebrate Diwali with his family and close relatives till November 16.

A three-judge bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana was seized of the matter arising from the October 3, 2021 incident in which five persons, including four farmers and a journalist, were killed after vehicles allegedly linked to Mishra's convoy ran over protesting farmers in Lakhimpur Kheri, Uttar Pradesh.
The farmers were agitating against the now-repealed farm laws.
The Court had earlier granted him bail subject to the condition that he not enter Lakhimpur Kheri except to appear in the trial.
The condition was later relaxed to permit him to visit his hometown on weekends.
Though bail was confirmed, the Court kept the matter pending to monitor the progress of the trial.

During today's hearing, Advocate Prashant Bhushan, appearing for the victims' side, expressed satisfaction with recent development regarding the transfer of the trial judge, on whom they had expressed a lack of confidence.
Senior Advocate Siddharth Dave, appearing for Ashish Mishra, submitted that the transfer was a routine administrative exercise and not based on any suspicion or adverse finding against the judge.
Chief Justice Surya Kant clarified that the Court was not casting any aspersions on anyone.
“We are not saying anything against anyone.
Whatever correctional measures the High Court has taken, good enough,” the CJI observed.
The Court had earlier directed the Allahabad High Court to take appropriate action on the report of the HC vigilance regarding the trial judge.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Asks SCBA Not To Declare Result Of November 2 General Body Meeting On Electoral Reforms
stories.title: Supreme Court Asks SCBA Not To Declare Result Of November 2 General Body Meeting On Electoral Reforms
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday allowed the Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) to hold its scheduled general body meeting on November 2 to discuss election reforms, but directed that voting must take place by secret ballot and that the outcome must not be declared.
The results are to be placed before the Court in a sealed envelope.

The directions were issued by a bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant after Senior Advocate Jaideep Gupta, who heads the Court-appointed committee examining the SCBA reform, made an oral mention and raised concerns over the proposed meeting.

Gupta pointed out that the SCBA had called a special general body meeting to pass two resolutions linked to the Court's May 29 order, one relating to proximity card entry and the other concerning veteran members, ahead of the November 5 hearing in the matter of SCBA v BD Kaushik(in which the Court is monitoring the SCBA electoral reforms).

Gupta submitted that while he was not opposing any resolution, the meeting was being convened without consultation and appeared to overreach the Court's order, especially since the matter is listed for hearing just three days later.
He also cautioned that any resolution passed would become binding immediately.

SCBA President Senior Advocate Pradeep Rai responded that the association wanted to ascertain the views of its members and that any concerns could have been resolved through discussion rather than approaching the Court.
“Instead of coming to this Court, we could have resolved it.
Why waste the valuable time of this Court?” Rai said, adding that the executive committee preferred consulting members before forming an opinion.
CJI Surya Kant clarified that the court-appointed committee's proposals aim to strengthen genuine practitioners rather than curtail their rights.
“Those who are genuinely regular visitors to the Supreme Court, having an interest in the Bar, the institution and the system, we want to strengthen their hands.
All those outsiders who have nothing to do with the profession should be isolated and excluded,” the Chief Justice observed.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Had 23 Years To Settle Legislative Privilege Vs Free Speech. It Chose Not To
stories.title: Supreme Court Had 23 Years To Settle Legislative Privilege Vs Free Speech. It Chose Not To
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: On October 6, 2026, a seven-judge bench of the Supreme Court disposed of one of the most significant constitutional references of the last two decades.
The question was straightforward: can a state legislature use its privileges under Article 194(3) to punish a journalist for what they write?
The answer, after 23 years: we will not say.
Not today.
Not in this case.
Come back when someone else gets arrested.
The reference arose from the N. Ravi case.
In April 2003, The Hindu published an editorial titled "Rising Intolerance," criticising the government of then Chief Minister J. Jayalalithaa.
The Tamil Nadu Assembly responded by passing a breach of privilege resolution.
On November 7, 2003, Speaker K. Kalimuthu found the editorial constituted a breach.
Police arrested five Hindu staff members within hours.
The Supreme Court stayed the arrests three days later, but the constitutional question of what happens when Article 194(3) collides with Article 19(1)(a) remained unresolved.

stories.title: HDFC Bank slips further as Bagchi takes charge amid leadership uncertainty
stories.summary: Bagchi inherits a bank under strain on multiple fronts; broader banking sector pressure added to the headwinds
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'takes charge' in title weight 40
article_sentences: HDFC Bank shares fell 0.71 per cent to ₹687.90 on the NSE by 12.15 pm Monday, extending the stock’s week-long slide as new chief executive Anup Bagchi formally assumed office.
Sellers dominated trade, accounting for 55.32 per cent of total quantity against buyers at 44.68 per cent, with traded volume reaching 115.52 lakh shares worth ₹797.01 crore.
The stock now sits just ₹6 above its 52-week low of ₹681.90, having shed nearly 31 per cent year-to-date against the Nifty 50’s 13.59 per cent decline over the same period.
The P/E ratio has compressed to 13.34, with the adjusted figure at 13.15.
Bagchi inherits a bank under strain on multiple fronts.
An internal probe into alleged disclosure of confidential information by two senior executives remains active and unresolved.
Deputy Managing Director Kaizad Bharucha is scheduled to exit by December, compounding the leadership transition.
Sashidhar Jagdishan, whom Bagchi succeeds, steps down after six years.

opening: HDFC Bank shares fell 0.71 per cent to ₹687.90 on the NSE by 12.15 pm Monday, extending the stock’s week-long slide as new chief executive Anup Bagchi formally assumed office.
Sellers dominated trade, accounting for 55.32 per cent of total quantity against buyers at 44.68 per cent, with traded volume reaching 115.52 lakh shares worth ₹797.01 crore.
body: The stock now sits just ₹6 above its 52-week low of ₹681.90, having shed nearly 31 per cent year-to-date against the Nifty 50’s 13.59 per cent decline over the same period.
The P/E ratio has compressed to 13.34, with the adjusted figure at 13.15.
Bagchi inherits a bank under strain on multiple fronts.
An internal probe into alleged disclosure of confidential information by two senior executives remains active and unresolved.
